blocks.content: Beyond the caching mechanics covered in the Docker Build module, a few additional techniques speed up the build process itself, particularly valuable in CI, where build time is a direct, recurring cost.

BuildKit, Docker's modern build engine, is smart enough to recognize when multi-stage build stages do not actually depend on each other, and builds those independent stages concurrently instead of strictly one after another, a real speedup for Dockerfiles with genuinely parallel stages.

blocks.alt: Independent stages run at the same time, not sequentially

blocks.content: 2. Cache Reuse, Recapped as a Speed Lever
blocks.text: 2. Cache Reuse, Recapped as a Speed Lever

blocks.content: As covered in depth in the Build Cache and Layer Caching topics, a warm cache turns a multi-minute build into one finishing in seconds, this remains the single highest-leverage build speed optimization available, worth re-emphasizing here specifically as a performance lever.

blocks.alt: The single biggest lever for build speed, revisited

blocks.content: 3. Why This Matters Most in CI
blocks.text: 3. Why This Matters Most in CI

blocks.content: A local build benefits from your machine's own cache naturally, a CI pipeline on ephemeral runners does not, unless you deliberately set up shared caching (covered in the Build Cache topic's --cache-from/--cache-to), every CI build effectively starts cold, paying the full build time on every single run.

blocks.alt: Shared CI cache turns every run from cold to warm

blocks.content: Building for multiple CPU architectures at once (x86 and ARM, for instance, common when supporting both traditional cloud instances and Apple Silicon development machines) with docker buildx builds each target platform concurrently rather than as separate, sequential build runs.

blocks.alt: Multiple target platforms, built concurrently, not one after another

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: BuildKit parallelizes independent multi-stage builds automatically, and a warm cache remains the single biggest lever for build speed.
CI pipelines need deliberate shared caching to avoid starting cold on every run, and buildx parallelizes multi-platform builds instead of running them sequentially.
